'''Philip Siu Lun Lee''' {{post-nominals|country=CAN|CM|OM}}<ref name="GG">{{cite web |url=http://gg.ca/honour.aspx?id=5021&t=12&ln=Lee |title=It's an Honour: Find a Recipient &ndash; Philip S. Lee, C.M., B.Sc., M.C.I.C. |work=The Governor General of Canada |publisher=Government of Canada |access-date=August 31, 2011}}</ref><ref name="OMB">{{Cite canlaw

|section     = 4, 6(1)
|subsection  =

|amended3    = S.M. 2011, c. 16, s. 45.
|amended4    = 
|amended5    = 
}} Retrieved August 31, 2011.</ref> (born May 5, 1944; [[Chinese language|Chinese]]: 李紹麟)<ref>[http://www.britishhongkong.com/cgi-bin/forum/YaBB.pl?num=1245671010/0#0http://www.mingpaotor.com/htm/News/20090620/tac1.htm Ming Pao Toronto]</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Marshall |first=Alison R. |date=December 22, 2009 |title=A Conversation with Winnipeg's Chinese Canadian Duet |journal=Manitoba History |issue=62 |pages=35–39 |location=Winnipeg |publisher=[[Manitoba Historical Society]] |format=fee required |issn=0226-5036 |access-date=August 31, 2011 |url=http://connection.ebscohost.com/c/articles/47434708 }}</ref> was the [[List of lieutenant governors of Manitoba#Lieutenant Governors of Manitoba, 1870-present|24th]] [[lieutenant governor of Manitoba]]. He was made a Member of the Order of Canada in 1999 and received the Queen's Golden Jubilee Medal in 2002.<ref name="pm" />
[[File:Philip S. Lee.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Philip S. Lee and Anita K. Lee at the 2010 Canada Day celebrations in Winnipeg]]

Born and raised in [[Hong Kong]], Lee migrated to Canada in 1962 to study at the [[University of Manitoba]].<ref name="pm" /> He graduated with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1966, and a public administration diploma in 1977.<ref name="rabson">{{cite news|url=http://www.winnipegfreepress.com/breakingnews/PM-names-Lee-as-Manitobas-new-Lieutenant-Governor-48615622.html|title=PM names Lee as Manitoba's new Lieutenant Governor|last=Rabson|first=Mia|date=June 19, 2009|newspaper=Winnipeg Free Press|access-date=August 4, 2009}}</ref> In 1967 he was hired by the City of [[Winnipeg]] as a research chemist.<ref name="pm">{{cite web|url=http://pm.gc.ca/eng/media.asp?id=2645|title=Backgrounder: Philip S. Lee, C.M.|date=19 June 2009|publisher=Office of the Prime Minister|access-date=2009-08-04|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100113230702/http://www.pm.gc.ca/eng/media.asp?id=2645|archive-date=13 January 2010}}</ref> He helped organize the Chinese pavilion in the first [[Folklorama]] in 1970 and later became Vice President of the Folk Arts Council of Winnipeg.<ref name="pm" /> In the [[1977 Manitoba general election]], Lee ran as a [[Progressive Conservative Party of Manitoba|Progressive Conservative]] candidate in [[Winnipeg Centre (provincial electoral division)|Winnipeg Centre]] where he lost to [[Bud Boyce]] of the [[Manitoba New Democratic Party]].  Lee was on Winnipeg's Refugee Assistance Committee from 1979 to 1986.<ref name="pm" /> He also advocated for the construction of the Winnipeg Chinese Cultural and Community Centre in the Dynasty Building, the Chinese Gate and Garden, and the Mandarin Building in Winnipeg.<ref name="pm" />

His appointment as Lieutenant Governor was made by [[Governor General of Canada]] [[Michaëlle Jean]], on the [[Advice (constitutional)|Constitutional advice]] of [[Prime Minister of Canada]] [[Stephen Harper]], on June 19, 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://news.gc.ca/web/article-eng.do?m=%2Findex&nid=460449 |title=Canada News Centre |access-date=22 June 2009 |archive-date=16 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716161907/http://news.gc.ca/web/article-eng.do?m=%2Findex&nid=460449 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Upon assuming the office on August 4, 2009, Lee became the 24th lieutenant governor of the province.<ref>{{cite news |title=Province makes history: First Lt.-Gov. of Chinese descent |first=Bruce |last=Owen |url=http://www.winnipegfreepress.com/local/province-makes-history-52508627.html |newspaper=Winnipeg Free Press |date=August 5, 2009 |at=section A, p. 5 |access-date=August 31, 2011 }}</ref> Lee left office on June 19, 2015, after a six-year term.

Lee was the third Chinese Canadian to be a provincial vice-regal, after [[David Lam (real estate entrepreneur)|David Lam]] of [[List of lieutenant governors of British Columbia|British Columbia]] and [[Norman Kwong]] of [[List of lieutenant governors of Alberta|Alberta]].

==Arms==
{{Infobox COA wide
|image          = Philip Siu Lun Lee Escutcheon.png
|year_adopted   = August 20, 2010
|crest          = Issuant from a circlet of prairie crocus flowers Or a plum tree Proper fructed Purpure.
|torse          = 
|escutcheon     = Chequy of nine Purpure and Argent on a chief Or three bauhinia flowers Purpure.
|supporters     = Dexter a sea-bison sinister a sea-qilin both Or queued Purpure.
|compartment    = Issuant from barry wavy Or and Purpure.
|motto          = Advance The People
|orders         = The ribbon and insignia of a Companion of the [[Order of Canada]].<br />'''DESIDERANTES MELIOREM PATRIAM''' ''(They desire a better country)''
|other_elements = 
|symbolism      = The nine-division pattern represents His Honour’s position as the ninth child of his parents. The bauhinia flower represents Hong Kong, the birthplace of His Honour and his wife, Anita. Three such flowers represent their three children. The plum colour is His Honour’s favourite colour. The prairie crocus flowers, the provincial flower coloured gold here, represent His Honour’s interest in the betterment of all Manitobans. The plum tree alludes to the name “Lee”, which means “plum tree” in Chinese. The bison is taken from the arms of Manitoba. The qilin is significant to His Honour’s family and Chinese heritage, representing benevolence, goodwill, and good government. The lower body of a fish-tail alludes to his skills in water research and limnology studies. Refers to the fact that His Honour has always been a community-minded supporter of encouraging the development and growth of all Manitobans.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://reg.gg.ca/heraldry/pub-reg/project-pic.asp?lang=e&ProjectID=2063&ProjectElementID=7227| last=Canadian Heraldic Authority| title=The Public Register of Arms, Flags, and Badges of Canada > Philip Siu Lun LEE| publisher=Queen's Printer for Canada| date=August 20, 2010| access-date=February 10, 2014}}</ref>
}}
